subject: Priority token pool request for launch weekend
messages:
From: Rajiv Singh <rajiv@stellanova.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@stellanova.ai
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Priority token pool request for launch weekend

Hi Vivek,

Quick note from our side — we have a hard launch for the new patient triage feature on Friday 2026-07-24 at 00:00 UTC and expect a large concentrated spike during the first 48 hours. Based on the test traffic and the staging runs (attached), estimated peak is ~1,800 requests/min with average generation of ~140 tokens per request. That maps to ~252k tokens/min peak.

We’re asking if Redwood can grant a temporary priority token pool (a carveout above our normal rate tier) and a short SLA amendment for the 48-hour window: 2026-07-24 00:00 UTC → 2026-07-26 00:00 UTC. Specifically: 1) reserve ~260k tokens/min burst capacity, 2) relax fairness throttling for our tenant in that window, and 3) a latency SLO of p95 ≤ 200ms for generation requests to the primary model.

This is critical to the launch experience — if our users get throttled/fairness-lowered responses during onboarding, conversion drops substantially. We’re prepared to accept a short-term surcharge or committed burst credits — we need to know feasibility and any gating items (e.g., SOC/PII review, change freeze approvals).

Attached: traffic_profile_q3.xlsx (high-level hourly projections).

Can we get confirmation by EOD Wed 2026-07-21 so we can lock in the rollout plan?

Thanks,
Rajiv
Rajiv Singh
VP Engineering, StellaNova Health
rajiv@stellanova.ai

---
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Singh <rajiv@stellanova.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Priority token pool request for launch weekend

Rajiv — thanks for the details and the spreadsheet. I’ve looped in Marissa (Account Lead) to coordinate the commercial/operational side. High level: we can usually support temporary priority pools but need to confirm a few items before we commit to the latency SLO and fairness override: 

- Confirm exact start/end in UTC and whether the window is flexible by +/- 6 hours.
- Confirm whether traffic contains special processing (LLM tools/calling) or PII-heavy content that would require additional review.
- Can you send a short hourly distribution for the two-day window (you already gave peak/min average; hourly shape helps us size buffer vs sustained).

Assuming the traffic profile you shared is representative, we’ll propose an operational plan: short-term priority token pool sized to peak + 10% buffer, temporary override of fairness policy for the window, and a canary/fallback routing rule to a quantized model if capacity is hit. I’ll need eng to sign off on the latency target being realistic for the primary model under the reserved pool.

Next steps: Marissa — can you kick off pricing/contract notes and coordinate with infra (Jonas) for capacity confirmation? Rajiv — if you can drop the per-hour expected tokens for the two days (CSV or Google Sheet), that’ll speed this up.

Happy to do a short sync tomorrow if helpful.

-Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Platform Sales | Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 12:02:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Priority token pool request for launch weekend

Marissa / Jonas — forwarding Rajiv’s request. Key asks from the customer: 260k tokens/min reserve for a 48h window starting 2026-07-24 00:00 UTC, temporary fairness override, and a p95 ≤ 200ms generation SLO. They can accept short-term credits/surcharge.

Jonas — can you validate feasibility and give me: 1) whether we can carve that much priority pool on Hosted for that customer without impacting fairness across others, 2) what fallback model and routing config we should pre-configure (suggest: quantized redwood-medium-v1), and 3) estimated perf numbers (p50/p95) under the reserved pool for their expected request shape?

Marissa — if feasible, I’ll propose a short mutual action plan and a one-off amendment for the window. Note: check SOC2/PII gating — Rajiv mentioned health data. If we need additional controls, call that out now.

I’ve attached my draft mutual_action_plan_draft.md for edits.

-Vivek

--- Original message attached below ---
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 16:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Priority token pool request for launch weekend

Vivek / Jonas — quick capacity note after reviewing traffic_profile_q3.xlsx and running a short simulation with infra: 

- Feasibility: Yes — we can stand up a temporary priority token pool for StellaNova on Hosted for the requested window. Recommend reserve = 250k tokens/min (slightly below their ask) with automated burst allowance up to 300k tokens/min controlled by the pool. Rationale: gives headroom while protecting overall cluster from indefinite exhaustion.

- Fairness override: we can apply a scoped override for their tenant limited strictly to the 48h window. Implement as a temporary policy that elevates their priority tag; we will also enable server-side circuit breakers that will route requests to a fallback model if observed sustained latency > 250ms for 5 consecutive minutes.

- Latency SLO: we can commit to operational target p95 ≤ 200ms for the primary model within the reserved pool under the simulated load, provided that: 1) the customer allows us to enable prefix caching and minimum batching controls (we’ll propose conservative batching settings), and 2) they accept an automated fallback to redwood-medium-v1 for degraded tail cases (fallback clearly communicated).

- Duration & timing: Start: 2026-07-24 00:00 UTC; End: 2026-07-26 00:00 UTC. Jonas: schedule a quick canary deployment on 07-23 to validate perf.

- Commercial: propose a short amendment capturing the exact reserve size, buffer, and a one-time burst fee (details to be drafted). Rajiv — we can include some upfront credits to offset the fee; Marissa will follow up with the exact numbers.

Attachments: capacity_plan_summary.pdf (sim results + suggested routing rules).

I’ll prepare the mutual action plan for Rajiv to sign off. Jonas — let me know if the fallback model tuning requires any additional infra work more than 24h.

-Marissa
